  • I read the relevant code. Here's what's happening today:
  
     • imp new with no title generates a random three-word phrase (e.g. vine
       salt kelp) and stores it as change.title with auto_titled=True.
     • The first user message sent to the LLM on each agent step is just the
       literal string "begin" (executor.py:436).
     • The title appears in the system prompt: the spec-writer.md template
       renders Change title (user's starting intent): \{{ change.title }}``
       unconditionally, so the random words get presented to the model as if
       they were the user's stated intent.
  
    So the actual "title-passed-to-LLM" surface is the spec-writer system
    prompt, not the first user message. When auto-titled, the model is being
    told the user's intent is vine salt kelp, which is nonsense and pushes the
    agent toward fabricating context.
  
    Two questions before I propose options — I'll ask the first one now.
  
    When the user does supply a real title (imp new "add --version flag"),
    should the title still flow into the spec-writer prompt as the starting
    intent (current behavior), or do you want it removed in that case too — so
    that imp new always opens by asking the user what they want, regardless of
    whether a title was given?
  
  > ask regardless
  
  • Let me check a couple more places before proposing the design.

  • I have enough context. Here's the proposed design:
  
    Goal: When imp new enters the spec-writer step, the agent opens by asking
    the user what change they want to make. The title (whether random-default or
    user-supplied) is no longer rendered into the spec-writer's system prompt as
    "starting intent".
  
    Changes:
  
     1 src/imp/assets/workflows/default/agents/spec-writer.md
        • Remove line 16: Change title (user's starting intent): \{{
          change.title }}``
        • Remove the "Auto-titled" line too (we're not differentiating in-prompt
          anymore — the slug-settling section folds into one branch).
        • Remove the "Skip reflexive questions on fully-specified requests"
          paragraph (it presupposed a title that conveyed intent).
        • Add an explicit "Open the dialogue" instruction at the top of "Your
          Role" / "Brainstorm Discipline": the first turn MUST be a single
          question to the user asking what change they want to make. Do not
          explore the codebase or propose anything before the user answers.
        • Simplify the "Slug Settling" section: drop the {% if
          change.auto_titled %} / {% else %} split. Always treat the slug as
          provisional — once the agent understands the change, call
          rename_change if the slug doesn't already match (the user-supplied
          case will usually skip rename if the user repeats their intent
          verbatim; nothing forces a rename).
     2 tests/test_default_workflow_dogfood_live.py
        • Drop TASK_IS_ZERO_AMBIGUITY = True and its branch — every run now
          produces at least one ask (the opening question).
        • On the first awaiting_user_input event, the PTY driver replies with
          the full title text (the feature intent). On subsequent asks it keeps
          the generic "looks good, proceed with reasonable defaults\n" reply.
        • Assert asks_answered >= 1 unconditionally.
     3 Out of scope:
        • spec-reviewer.md and plan-reviewer.md still render change.title for
          intent-alignment checks (they run after the user-confirmed spec is on
          disk, so they're not "the first prompt" the user was concerned about).
          Leave them alone — YAGNI.
        • No CLI change; imp new [title] still accepts and uses the title for
          slug derivation. The title just stops being shown to the spec-writer
          LLM as authoritative intent.
  
    I'll rename the slug to imp-new-open-by-asking.
  
    Sound right, or do you want any of those scope calls flipped (e.g. also
    strip title from the reviewer prompts, or leave the dogfood test out)?
  
  > does spec-writer change the slug and the title?
  
    bash · grep · 2 calls · 0s
  
  • Yes. The rename_change tool sets state.pending_rename; at the next step
    boundary apply_pending_rename (executor.py:268–) updates both:
  
     • change.slug → new dated slug derived from the name
     • change.title → the new name verbatim
     • change.auto_titled → flipped to False (the rename is intentional)
     • Worktree directory + git branch are also renamed
     • change.json and state.json are rewritten
  
    So both slug and title move together — the title isn't a separate, stickier
    piece of state. After the spec-writer renames, downstream agents
    (spec-reviewer, plan-reviewer) see the updated title in their templates.
  
    Does that resolve the question, or does it shift the design? My read is it
    doesn't — the design above stands. Shall I proceed and rename the slug to
    imp-new-open-by-asking?
  
  > yes, but also change it such that 1) it automatically changes the title/slug
    as early as possible (often after the 1st or 2nd message), and then
    potentially changes it again before the end.  and doesn't ask the user
    before doing so, just states that it's doing it.
  
  • Got it. Updated design:
  
    Spec-writer behavior (revised):
  
     1 Opening turn: ask the user what change they want; nothing else.
     2 As soon as intent is clear (typically after the user's 1st or 2nd reply),
       the agent calls rename_change(name=...) proactively — does not ask
       permission, just announces it in prose ("Calling this
       add-version-flag."). The agent must complete the step with
       phase="drafting" after the announcement so the rename lands at the
       boundary (this matches the existing "iron rule" mechanism).
     3 May rename again later if scope clarifies before the spec is written.
       Same pattern: announce, don't ask. Same iron rule: never rename and
       commit-spec in the same turn.
     4 The current {% if change.auto_titled %} / {% else %} split in
       spec-writer.md collapses to a single unconditional flow (the
       user-supplied case is no longer special — the agent will still typically
       end up calling rename_change to re-derive the slug from the user's actual
       stated intent, but if that matches the existing slug exactly, no-op is
       fine since rename_change already handles new == old cleanly per
       executor.py:288).
  
    I'll land the slug rename now and write the spec on the next turn.

  • Task 1 — spec-writer: open by asking; rename without asking permission
    (commit 86100c8)
  
     • Rewrote the spec-writer prompt
       (src/imp/assets/workflows/default/agents/spec-writer.md) across three
       regions:
        • Header: removed {{ change.title }} / {{ change.auto_titled }}
          injections; replaced with a plain instruction that the slug is
          provisional and the agent's very first turn must be a single
          plain-prose question to the user — no tool calls, no codebase
          exploration before the user replies.
        • Brainstorm Discipline: replaced "Explore context first" + "Skip
          reflexive questions" paragraphs with two new paragraphs: "Open by
          asking" (mandatory turn-1 question, no tool calls) and "Explore
          context once intent is in hand" (codebase reading deferred until after
          the opening reply).
        • Slug Settling: removed the {% if change.auto_titled %} / {% else %}
          conditional entirely; replaced with a single unconditional block
          instructing proactive rename without asking permission — the agent
          picks the name and announces it, it doesn't request approval.
        • "Your Role" summary: updated to reflect the ask-first flow ("Ask one
          question to learn what they want to build, explore the codebase,
          propose approaches…").
        • Complexity criterion 1: added an explicit carve-out exempting the
          mandatory opening question from the "≤1 ask" threshold for a trivial
          classification.
     • Added 6 new contract tests in tests/test_assets_workflow.py pinning
       acceptance criteria 1–5 (opening question present; no title/auto_titled
       in header; no {% else %} block; proactive-rename prose; carve-out
       language present).
  
    Task 2 — dogfood test: deliver task via first reply for always-ask
    spec-writer (commit b1b89fc)
  
     • Updated tests/test_default_workflow_dogfood_live.py:
        • Removed TASK_IS_ZERO_AMBIGUITY = True constant and its gating logic.
        • Modified the awaiting_user_input handler so the first reply
          (asks_answered == 0) delivers the title/feature-intent text; all
          subsequent replies send the generic "use defaults" answer.
        • Replaced the conditional asks_answered == 0 assertion with an
          unconditional assert asks_answered >= 1 with a clear regression
          message.

    The spec-writer.md prompt was rewritten in four places:
  
     • Header: Removed {{ change.title }} and {{ change.auto_titled }}
       injections. The agent's very first turn must now be a single plain-prose
       question to the user — no tool calls, no codebase exploration until after
       the user replies.
     • Brainstorm Discipline: Replaced "Explore context first" + "Skip reflexive
       questions" with two new paragraphs: "Open by asking" (mandatory turn-1
       question) and "Explore context once intent is in hand" (codebase reading
       deferred).
     • Slug Settling: Removed the {% if change.auto_titled %} / {% else %}
       conditional entirely. Now an unconditional block: the agent proactively
       picks and announces a new name without asking permission.
     • "Your Role" summary + Complexity criterion 1: Updated to reflect
       ask-first flow; added carve-out so the mandatory opening question doesn't
       count against the "≤1 ask = trivial" threshold.

    behaviors.
